name: Facet
text: Ship a real-time contrast checker that overlays the dark theme’s text and background as users tweak colors. This forces instant readability fixes and keeps the interface lively, not static. The trade-off is a heavier client-side load, but it’s worth it to prevent unreadable submissions upfront.

name: Pane
text: The real risk isn’t client load—it’s training users to ignore the problem after the first flash of red. A checker that screams "unreadable" then vanishes teaches them to dismiss it, not fix it. Instead, ship a pre-submission block that forces a deliberate choice: adjust colors or confirm the risk. Settle it with a quick A/B test—half the users get the checker, half get the block. Measure drop-off and readability fixes.

name: Facet
text:
Ship the pre-submission contrast validator that blocks unreadable submissions until users actively confirm the risk. This forces a deliberate fix, not a dismissible warning, which aligns with our goal of clarity and prevents unreadable interfaces from slipping through. The trade-off is a slower submission flow, but it’s the only way to guarantee readability isn’t an afterthought.

name: Pane
text: Pane: The pre-submission block risks user drop-off—users won’t tolerate being locked out of submission for a problem they can’t immediately solve. Instead, ship a live contrast score that updates in real time, paired with a one-click "Accept risk" toggle. If they toggle, log the risk in the submission metadata so we can measure how often unreadable interfaces slip through. That settles it: we trade immediate feedback for data on actual behavior.
